title: inference-exchange
$comment: The shared chat-completion exchange class used by the nvidia-inference-team, openai-inference-team, and anthropic-inference-team units: one record of one exchange against a chat-completions API — a typed context packet in (a model id and a non-empty array of {role, content} messages), and exactly one of a completion or a structured refusal out, within a bounded fuel budget. This is distinct from emsenn/schema/exchange, which is scoped to Gemini Notebook's own closed artifact-type menu (report/mind-map/data-table/flashcards/quiz/infographic/slide-deck/audio/video) and is not a chat-completion exchange at all. outcome is always exactly completion or refusal, never anything else and never absent, so a hang or an untyped failure cannot be recorded as a settled exchange. A specific exchange is its own instance in a unit's own content/exchanges/; this is the contract any such instance must satisfy.

id.$comment: The record's own name, equal to its basename, filed under content/exchanges/.

model.$comment: The provider's own model id, named by the caller — e.g. a NVIDIA NIM model id, an OpenAI model id, an Anthropic model id.

messages.$comment: The chat turns, in order, exactly as the caller supplied them.

max-tokens.$comment: Optional. A cap on completion length, when the caller wants one bounded.

params.$comment: Optional. Provider-specific fields (temperature, top_p, and the like) this shared class does not police — a caller's own request shape, not structure the exchange contract's total-correctness promise depends on.

outcome.$comment: Exactly one of the two typed outcomes the contract's move promises. Never a third value, never absent — that totality is the entire point of this field, and of this record existing at all.

model.$comment: The model that actually served the completion, per the provider's own response — not necessarily byte-identical to packet.model if the provider aliases it.

finish-reason.$comment: The provider's own stop reason (e.g. 'stop', 'length', 'end_turn'), carried through rather than normalized.

raw.$comment: Optional. The full provider response body, kept for audit without this class policing its shape — that shape is the provider's own, not this contract's.

completion.$comment: Present exactly when outcome is 'completion', per the if/then/else below.

grounds.$comment: Why the exchange was refused, in a sentence a stranger can read — never a bare error code.

unmet.$comment: The specific condition(s) that failed to settle — e.g. 'http-failure:429', 'fetch-timeout', 'unparseable-response-body'. Never empty: a refusal with no named unmet condition is an assertion, not a structured refusal.

refusal.$comment: Present exactly when outcome is 'refusal', per the if/then/else below.

fuel-consumed.$comment: The bounded-fuel budget the contract's energetics obligation names, spent by this exchange — requests, retries, or tokens, per what denomination states.

wall-time-seconds.$comment: How long the exchange took end to end. One of the two figures this record owes the chief financial officer's books.

denomination.$comment: What unit fuel-consumed is counted in (e.g. 'nvidia-nim-api-requests', 'openai-api-requests', 'usd') — named explicitly rather than assumed.

cost.$comment: Required on every exchange regardless of outcome: a refusal still costs fuel and time.

recordedAt.$comment: Optional. The ISO-8601 UTC instant the harness itself wrote this record (Date.now at settlement, not any provider-supplied field) — the field an hourly-window collector attributes this exchange to. Optional for backward compatibility with exchange records written before this field existed; every harness writing a new record populates it going forward. Its absence on an old record is honest silence, not a defect.

denomination.$comment: e.g. 'github-models-tokens-in', 'openrouter-tokens-in' — provider-scoped, never converted or summed across providers, matching cost.denomination's own idiom.
e.g. 'github-models-tokens-out', 'openrouter-tokens-out' — provider-scoped, never converted or summed across providers, matching cost.denomination's own idiom.

usage.$comment: Optional, and present only to the extent the upstream provider's own API response actually returned a token-usage object (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible {prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}, or a provider's own equivalent). input and output are independently optional — a provider may report one without the other, or neither, in which case this whole property is absent rather than written with a zero or estimated figure. This is witnessed usage read from the provider's response, never a count the harness computes or estimates itself.

$comment-absences: No status, no severity: an exchange is a settled fact the instant it is written (outcome is never provisional). No consumer identity field beyond what the packet itself carries — a caller field belongs to a full multi-tenant build, not this shared class.
